LESSON: VOLLEYBALL

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.3: Volleyball

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Volleyball. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can service skills in Volleyball be used to win a game?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the serving and the digging skills in Volleyball
2. perform under-arm service for skill acquisition
3. appreciate playing Volleyball game for enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: VOLLEYBALL
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Volleyball helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: VOLLEYBALL
Study Volleyball like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the serving and the digging skills in Volleyball

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the serving and the digging skills in Volleyball. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the serving and the digging skills in Volleyball.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Volleyball” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the serving and the digging skills in Volleyball. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Perform under-arm service for skill acquisition

What this means
In this part you learn to perform under-arm service for skill acquisition. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform under-arm service for skill acquisition.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Volleyball in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform under-arm service for skill acquisition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate playing Volleyball game for enjoyment

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate playing Volleyball game for enjoyment. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate playing Volleyball game for enjoyment.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate playing Volleyball game for enjoyment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Volleyball is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Volleyball” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify the serving and the digging skills in Volleyball)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Volleyball in your own words. (skill: perform under-arm service for skill acquisition)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate playing Volleyball game for enjoyment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Volleyball to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the serving and the digging skills in Volleyball.
3. Practise this skill: perform under-arm service for skill acquisition.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate playing Volleyball game for enjoyment.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Volleyball from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Volleyball: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Volleyball?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can service skills in Volleyball be used to win a game?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Volleyball means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the serving and the digging skills in Volleyball.
5. Be able to: perform under-arm service for skill acquisition.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
